checks_run.procedure: D-214 open question on BE-Z6: does the re-raise rule hide a real conflict, lose a system update, or let a stale human write overwrite a newer human one? I read rebaseOverSystemOccurrences, the 0101 guard and history trigger, and the raise paths, then ran my own integration probe (Q1-Q6) next to the candidate's exception-recurrence-race.test.ts.
checks_run.command: tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project integration apps/api/test/integration/operations/zz-qa-dg6r5-exception-rebase.test.ts apps/api/test/integration/operations/exception-recurrence-race.test.ts
checks_run.environment: Scratch clone r5m; disposable PostgreSQL 16.15; ports 30130-30131
checks_run.expected: A rebase is accepted only over system recurrences; occurrence fields are kept; human-vs-human stays 409; refusals write nothing.
checks_run.actual:
The rule itself is sound. The candidate's race test passes 7/7.
- Q1: after 3 recurrences, an acknowledge with the version loaded before them keeps count 4, the last message and last_occurred_at (no system update lost), and steps the version once.
- Q6: the audit event records prior 4, new 5 and based_on_version {from 1, to 4}; an exact If-Match writes no based_on_version.
- Q2+Q3: two humans act concurrently on the same stale version after recurrences. In 5 of 5 rounds exactly one gets 200 and the other 409, with one human event.
- Q3b: a stale resolve after another human's acknowledge plus recurrences is 409, and the row is unchanged.
- Q4: a recurrence attributed to a user is not treated as a system one (409, conservative).
- Q5: If-Match 0, -1, "abc", W/"1", "1.5" and * give 400; a far-ahead version gives 409; nothing is written.
The trigger classifies 'recurred' only when the status is unchanged, and the guard forbids changing an acknowledgement, so a recurrence can never carry a human's change.
Q2 FAILED, and the probe exits 1 by design. With 20 recurrences concurrent with a rebased acknowledge, the acknowledge succeeded but 2 of the 20 RAISES were rejected: 'operational_exception: each recurrence counts once and moves last_occurred_at forward'. The final count was 19 of 21. That is not BE-Z6's rule; it is a pre-existing defect in the raise path, raised as F-DG6-380 (see QA-R5-14b).

checks_run.procedure: Follow-up of QA-R5-14 Q2 (A13 'failed jobs remain recoverable', REQ-S12-019, D-203 concurrency). The worker's own captureJobFailure, which worker.ts runs after a job's last failed attempt inside runJobBatch, is called concurrently for N distinct jobs of ONE queue. N = 8 and N = 4 (the default WORKER_JOB_CONCURRENCY), 5 rounds each, with the exception not yet open and already open. Then the failure-queue rows and the exception's occurrences are counted. Control: a scratch copy with only the two last_occurred_at expressions changed.
checks_run.command: tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project integration apps/api/test/integration/operations/zz-qa-dg6r5-concurrent-job-failure.test.ts
checks_run.environment: Scratch clone r5m (candidate code; the control is a separate, labelled change, reverted afterwards); disposable PostgreSQL 16.15; ports 30132-30134
checks_run.expected: Every failure is captured exactly once: N operational_failure rows, N occurrences, 0 rejected captures.
checks_run.actual:
FAIL on the candidate:
- N = 8 (14b): every one of 10 bursts lost captures, for example 'rejected 5; operational_failure rows 3 (expected 8); occurrences 3'.
- N = 4 (14d): 9 of 10 bursts lost 1 or 2 of 4.
- The reason is always the 0101 guard's 'each recurrence counts once and moves last_occurred_at forward'.
Cause: the raise writes greatest(now(), ${current.last_occurred_at}::timestamptz) with the stored value passed back as a millisecond JavaScript Date. A raise that commits second but started first therefore moves last_occurred_at backwards by the truncated microseconds, and the guard rolls back the whole captureJobFailure transaction: the failure-queue row, the occurrence and the job.failed event.
Control (14c, NOT the candidate): with the column reference greatest(now(), operational_exception.last_occurred_at), all 10 bursts capture 8/8 and 9/9, and QA-R5-14 Q2 has 0 rejections.
This is F-DG6-380: High, mandatory (data integrity on the A13 recoverability path). It predates BE-Z6, since the raise code is unchanged since round 4, and no candidate test fails jobs concurrently on one queue.

checks_run.procedure: D-214 open question on BE-Z5's declared residuals (handback §10), judged against ADR-0051 §2, its 2026-11-04 amendment and D-195 Q3. I read restricted.ts, blocker-escalation.ts and the sweep test, took the sweep's logged list of unfillable operations from this round's run, and checked the benefit-named ones.
checks_run.environment: Clone; integration run 1 log
checks_run.expected: Each residual either shows no sensitive benefit's code, title or value to a non-admitted reader, or is a disclosed environmental or data gap.
checks_run.actual:
Each one is acceptable; none is a finding.
(1) 71 unfillable GETs (logged by name; 418 requests per reader). Of them only getBenefitOverlap, getBenefitScenario, getTransitionDecision and getBenefitGroup name benefits. The first three are path-guarded by SENSITIVE_REACH_PARAMS with their own passing tests. getBenefitGroup (benefits/groups.ts presentGroups) returns only memberBenefitIds and countedBenefitId, never a benefit's title or values, and the swept listBenefitGroups returns the same DTO. The KPI restatement operations are KPI-derived.
(2) The search index is not exercised by the sweep. The ask's search document now indexes the neutral title, and search is filtered by the ReadScope (BE-B), which A12's search tests prove (a12-p6-scope-isolation passes).
(3) Stored rows from before the fix: no released environment exists. That is a data-migration decision, not a product defect on this candidate.
(4) Benefit ids in the frozen G6 snapshot: ADR-0051 treats ids as non-content (the inbox redaction keeps ids), and round 3 accepted them.
(5) Counts kept as truthful verdicts: the D-195 Q3 totals rule; hiddenItemCount is a DG4 contract field (ADR-0036); the frozen itemCount, the G6 placeholder and benefit_missing show no code, title or value.
The sweep scans response bodies of ANY status for the title, the 'code title' label and the planned value, so free text in report sections is covered wherever the sweep reaches.

summary: FAIL on candidate 832e5c82 (2740 files, source d7b21bad). My open finding F-DG6-320 is CLOSED_VERIFIED: a real kpi.stale exception (production worker) and the heartbeat exception both show en and ar catalogue text, and four mutants are caught by problems-all.test.ts. Every candidate test passes, after re-runs for load timeouts and for side effects of my own: static checks, unit in all four Node and locale combinations, integration twice (422 files; 4238 passed in run 2), tests/qa alone, product journeys (276 per language and locale setting), root acceptance with loopback-only connections, a22-p6-operability 16/16, demo, probes, and a provisional load run with every class within target. BE-Z5's residuals are acceptable, and BE-Z6's rebase rule neither hides conflicts nor loses updates. New finding F-DG6-380 (High, mandatory): concurrent last-attempt job failures on one queue lose their failure-queue rows, because the exception recurrence fails its occurrence guard (a millisecond-truncated timestamp) and rolls back the capture. That breaks A13 'failed jobs remain recoverable' (REQ-S20-013), so the verdict is FAIL. All data is synthetic, and nothing here is a G1-G6 business approval; product G6 never implies DG7.
